Hi Mike,

Sorry about that. I can definitely recreate the issue. I'm going to try to pinpoint what's wrong with the generated code.

If I find a work around, I'll let you know.


Daniel


On Wed, Aug 31, 2016 at 5:22 PM, Mike Beddo <mbe...@gmail.com> wrote:
I've been working on a generalized Bass model for about two weeks. I think I have a change point in some data series, so I followed the advice in the Stan manual section 12.2. I haven't figured out how to use the dynamic programming "trick" in my case because my rates aren't constant, so I use nested for loops. I'm getting compile errors:

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) : 
  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! file140c57d0281e.cpp: In member function 'T__ model140c51727a5_bass_change_point_namespace::model140c51727a5_bass_change_point::log_prob(std::vector<T2>&, std::vector<int>&, std::ostream*) const [with bool propto__ = true, bool jacobian__ = true, T__ = stan::math::var, std::ostream = std::basic_ostream<char>]':
C:/Users/meb/Documents/R/win-library/3.2/StanHeaders/include/src/stan/model/util.hpp:108:39:   instantiated from 'double stan::model::log_prob_grad(const M&, std::vector<double>&, std::vector<int>&, std::vector<double>&, std::ostream*) [with bool propto = true, bool jacobian_adjust_transform = true, M = model140c51727a5_bass_change_point_namespace::model140c51727a5_bass_change_point, std::ostream = std::basic_ostream<char>]'
C:/Users/meb/Documents/R/win-library/3.2/rstan/include/rstan/stan_fit.hpp:1464:9:   instantiated from 'SEXPREC* rstan::stan_fit<Model, RNG_t>::grad_log_prob(SEXP, SEXP) [with Model = model140c51
In addition: Warning message:
running command 'C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-32~1.4RE/bin/x64/R CMD SHLIB file140c57d0281e.cpp 2> file140c57d0281e.cpp.err.txt' had status 1

I am hoping someone can point me to my problem (my model is pasted at bottom). I had the model working before I added the marginalization over the change point portion (these are highlighted below).

Here is the output of sessionInfo():

R version 3.2.4 Revised (2016-03-16 r70336)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 7 x64 (build 7601) Service Pack 1

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252  LC_CTYPE=English_United States.1252    LC_MONETARY=English_United States.1252
[4] LC_NUMERIC=C                           LC_TIME=English_United States.1252    

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] rstan_2.11.1       StanHeaders_2.11.0 ggplot2_2.1.0     

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] Rcpp_0.12.3      bitops_1.0-6     grid_3.2.4       plyr_1.8.3       jsonlite_0.9.19  gtable_0.2.0     stats4_3.2.4    
 [8] scales_0.4.0     statmod_1.4.24   tools_3.2.4      munsell_0.4.3    RCurl_1.95-4.8   rsconnect_0.4.3  inline_0.3.14   
[15] colorspace_1.2-6 h2o_3.8.3.2      gridExtra_2.2.1 

Here is my model. The function G1 (before change point) follows from the new buyer rate dN(t)/dt = p(M - N(t)), where M is ultimate potential and N is cumulative buyers at time t. The function G2 (after change point) follows from the new buyer rate dN(t)/dt = (p + q*N/M)(M - N).

functions {
  real G1(real xt, real p) {
    return 1 - exp(-p*xt);
  }
  
  real G2(real xt, real p, real q, real xt_s) {
    real f;
    real K;
    real fac;
    
    f = 1 - exp(-p*xt_s);
    K = (1 + q/p*f)/(1 - f);
    fac = exp(-(p+q)*(xt - xt_s));
    
    return (K - fac)/(K + q/p*fac);
  }
}

data {
  int<lower=1> T;                 // number of weeks since rollout
  int<lower=0> hhs[T];         // count of new buyers for product and week number
  real<lower=0>price[T];    // product price by week number
}

transformed data {
  real sum_N;
  vector[T] rel_price;
  real log_unif;
  
  sum_N = sum(hhs);
  rel_price = to_vector(price)/price[1];
  log_unif = -log(T+1);
}

parameters {
  real alpha;
  real beta;
  real<lower=0> epsilon;
  real M;
  real<lower=-1> d;        // product level first-week displays
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[T+1] lp;
  real p;
  real q;    // q can be negative, but p + q >= 0 always (for physical solutions)
  real e;

  p = inv_logit(alpha);
  q = (1 + p)*inv_logit(beta) - p;   // -p <= q <= 1
  e = -epsilon;
  
  lp = rep_vector(log_unif, T+1);
  
  {
    real xt;
    real xt_last;
    real xt_chg;
    real mu;

    // sure wish I could figure out a way to do this with
    // a dynamic program, but mu depends on price-time integral.
    for (s in 0:T) {
      xt_last = 0;
      xt_chg = 0;

      for (t in 1:T) {
        if (rel_price[t] == 0)
          continue;
        else
          xt = pow(rel_price[t], e) + (t == 1 ? d : 0);

        if (t <= s)      
          mu = G1(xt, p) - G1(xt_last, p);
        else
          mu = G2(xt, p, q, xt_chg) - G2(xt_last, p, q, xt_chg);
      
        lp[s+1] = lp[s+1] + poisson_lpmf(hhs[t] | mu);
        
        xt_last = xt_last + xt;
        if (t == s)
          xt_chg = xt_last;
      }
    }
  }
}

model {
  M ~ pareto(sum_N, 1);
  d ~ normal(0, 5);
  
  alpha ~ normal(-3, 1);                        // meta-analyses show p = 0.03

  beta ~ normal(-0.5, 1);                      // meta-analyses show q = 0.38

  epsilon ~ normal(0, 5);           // prior is elasticity no bigger than around 5

  target += log_sum_exp(lp);
}

generated quantities {
  int<lower=1,upper=T+1> s;
  s = categorical_rng(softmax(lp));
}

parts:
Hi Mike,

I found a workaround. There is a bug in the Stan compiler (translates Stan language to C++) and I'll open up an issue shortly.

It looks like an issue with the tenary operator. If you replace this line:

with this:
if (t == 1)
  xt = pow(rel_price[t], e) + d;
else
  xt = pow(rel_price[t], e);

it'll compile.



Daniel
